summary: ReactiveUI.Binding 8.6.0 compile-time binding generation for ReactiveUI 25.0.1 observation, binding, trimming, and AOT.
recommendedPatterns: Keep binding lambdas inline and simple so compile-time generation can optimize them.
Prefer compile-time bindings when AOT, trimming, or startup performance matters.
Use platform-specific binding packages where needed.
Fix all RXUIBIND diagnostics before running: unsupported generated call sites may throw at runtime.
avoidPatterns: Do not hide binding expressions behind variables or indirection that breaks generator analysis.
Do not mix runtime and compile-time binding styles without team conventions.
Do not combine ReactiveUI.Binding and ReactiveUI.Binding.Reactive in the same application.
setupSteps: Add ReactiveUI.Binding and any required platform package.
Watch diagnostics after refactors and renames.
Use the ReactiveUI.Binding.Reactive family instead of the lean family only when preserving System.Reactive APIs.
commonPitfalls: Assuming classic runtime binding idioms will all translate to generator-optimized code.
Reflection-based ViewModel discovery in WhenActivated is not trim-safe; pass an explicit ViewModel observable.

features: Compile-time one-way/two-way binding and command binding
Generated per-type observation factories and per-call-site dispatch
options: Lean built-in observable or .Reactive scheduler adapter
WPF, WinForms, or MAUI platform package
packageSelection: ReactiveUI 25.0.1 uses ReactiveUI.Binding 8.6.0; the generator/analyzers are included automatically.
Choose ReactiveUI.Binding.Reactive instead of the lean package only for IScheduler/System.Reactive compatibility; do not install both flavors.
Add ReactiveUI.Binding.Wpf, ReactiveUI.Binding.WinForms, or ReactiveUI.Binding.Maui for platform notification support.
ReactiveUI.Binding.SourceGenerators is a compatibility package; new projects install the runtime package.
sourceGeneratorGuidance: Primary choice for static simple property observation/binding paths.
Fix every RXUIBIND diagnostic: a generated call site without valid output may throw at runtime.
Use runtime/manual binding only for unsupported indexers, fields, method calls, or genuinely dynamic member paths.
compatibilityNotes: The base package has no System.Reactive dependency; .Reactive provides scheduler/Rx compatibility.
In ReactiveUI 25.0.1 IInteraction<TInput,TOutput>.Handle(input) again returns IObservable<TOutput>; Interaction<TInput,TOutput>.WhenHandled(input) also returns an observable.
IViewFor, Interaction, ObservableAsPropertyHelper, and related binding types live in ReactiveUI.Binding (or ReactiveUI.Binding.Reactive).
Supported paths are simple property-access chains; RXUIBIND diagnostics identify unsupported expressions.
Notification factories cover INotifyPropertyChanged/IReactiveObject and supported platform dependency/KVO/component mechanisms.
migrationGuidance: Install ReactiveUI.Binding and keep binding lambdas inline so the generator can identify the call site.
Resolve all RXUIBIND diagnostics; make private controls visible internally to generated code or use an Unsafe overload when required.
Pass an explicit ViewModel observable to WhenActivated in trimmed applications; review handwritten IReactiveObject notification and binding write-thread behavior.
Choose ReactiveUI.Binding.Reactive only where existing public APIs or schedulers require System.Reactive compatibility.
